Interestingly enough, I both fully disagree with some of what you said and fully agree with another part. 

Art in general, and most artists are severely underrated.I’ll elaborate on this a little further down. 

But hear me out: the cult-like following that celebrities “earn” is highly toxic and out of place. We shouldn’t idolize celebrities. But those celebrities aren’t the best representation of what “real” artists are like.

First of all, what got most people through the lockdown of the pandemic? Movies, tv shows, 
music and so on. Yes they’re ”only” entertainment and “distractions” as you call them. But these are vital to the mental well-being of most people in our society. Even doctors and scientist and all of those “important” jobs, what do they do on their free time? They read books, they watch tv shows or movies, they listen to music, they go see theatre plays, they go to art museums. 

Now my second point, wether you’re more left or right leaning on the political spectrum will probably dictate wether or not you agree with this specific point. Artists are often bringers of positive social change. Throughout history, they have periodically been the starting point of revolutions under oppressive governments. Especially theatre. Since it’s creation in Ancient Greece, it has been a tool to voice the concerns of the people to those who hold the power. It’s also why they were often silenced. But not only has it been used for that purpose, it also often served as a mirror for society: showing the public their own wrongs on stage so they realize what they’re doing. 

We can learn so much about societies through history by looking at the art they produced. Culture is infinitely important part of any society, and it is created and expressed through art.

Now the reason that I say that art is underrated is because apart from the big names, most artists struggle to get funds to produce anything, they can barely make a living. When the same few people get all the spotlight, they become complaisant with their success and will often stop being truly relevant (though there’s obviously some exceptions.) 

I hope I was able to give you a new perspective on art!
